label: At D1, update gate is high after reaching S2, lower after reward or choosing a2.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_common==1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (trial == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("reward", -2)==1) * (prev_reward==1) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo
explanation: Raw z of unit 38 is large only at D1 (~0.5-0.7, rising over the episode) and near zero at GO/D2; its magnitude beyond timing is set at D1 by the previous trial: reached state S2 raises it strongly (~+0.44), a rewarded previous trial lowers it (~-0.18), and having chosen a2 lowers it (~-0.13), so a1->S2 unrewarded is highest and a2->S1 rewarded lowest. GO/D2 variation is tiny. Belief log-odds adds almost nothing once last trial is known; the trial before adds nothing. The free fit gains mainly from a window-first-trial indicator (no previous trial in the window, activation high), likely an artifact of window start. No future, hidden or model-output variables used.

issues: The direction claims check out. The D1 residuals by last trial are a1 S2 u +0.337 (highest), a2 S2 u +0.315, a1 S2 r +0.215, a2 S2 r +0.161, a1 S1 u -0.04, a2 S1 u -0.19, a1 S1 r -0.276 and a2 S1 r -0.388 (lowest). GO and D2 residuals are all under 0.06.

The reward and a2 effects are not additive, as the short form assumes. Reward lowers z by about 0.20 to 0.24 after S1 but only about 0.12 to 0.15 after S2. Choosing a2 lowers z by about 0.11 to 0.15 after S1 but only about 0.02 to 0.05 after S2. Misses on the recorded form show systematic D1 cell errors of about 0.1: after a1 S2 u it over-predicts by 0.097, after a1 S1 r by 0.096 and after a2 S1 r by 0.080; after '?' (no previous trial) it under-predicts by 0.118.

The recorded form scores 0.690 on test, against 0.78 for the additive last-trial table. Restricting the reward term to S1 trials, (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state == 1), raises it to 0.737 on test (weights +0.33, -0.27, -0.14). Restricting the a2 term to S1 instead gives 0.712; using prev_common instead of prev_action gives 0.680. Dropping the a2 term gives 0.643.

Adding belief_lo on top of the last trial adds almost nothing (0.648 vs 0.643), which supports the claim that belief does not matter. A trial==0 indicator adds 0.07 (0.714), which is consistent with the window-start effect the explanation describes.

Even with the better form, D1 cells still miss by about 0.12 (a1 S2 r over-predicted, a2 S2 u under-predicted). The worst-fit windows also show a strong window-start transient: the first D1 is about 0.8 to 0.9 against a prediction of about 0.45. The fit is good but not complete.
